_comment: CAMS Phase 18 curated matching-evaluation dataset. All skill names below are exact, case-sensitive matches against the live ESCO-derived skills table (verified against V10-V12 migrations) - seed_dataset.py resolves them by exact name after a substring search and fails loudly on any miss. Deliberately excluded from every skills[] list: 'Spring Boot', 'Django', 'Kotlin', 'Selenium', 'GraphQL' - none exist in the seeded vocabulary (confirmed absent from V10/V11/V12), so they only ever appear in free-text description fields. backend-java-1 is the designated ESCO-gap query candidate for brief Section 3.6: its real Spring Boot experience is only readable in its description, never as a structured skill, mirrored by the backend-spring-1 listing which needs Spring Boot in its own description while its structured skills[] can only say 'Java (computer programming)'.

candidates.headline: Backend Java developer
candidates.description: Six years building backend services in Java, almost all of it with Spring Boot - REST APIs, message-driven microservices with Kafka, and PostgreSQL-backed persistence. Comfortable owning a service from design through production, writing integration tests, and containerizing with Docker for deployment.

candidates.headline: Backend Python developer
candidates.description: Backend engineer specializing in Python web services, mostly Django, with PostgreSQL as the primary datastore and Docker for local dev and CI. Also comfortable with AWS for deployment - RDS, ECS and S3 in past roles.

candidates.headline: Senior React developer
candidates.description: Frontend specialist with five years of React in production - hooks, context, React Query, and a fair amount of performance tuning on large component trees. Strong TypeScript, comfortable owning a design system built on top of plain CSS and HTML.

candidates.headline: Frontend developer, Angular
candidates.description: Three years building enterprise dashboards in Angular with TypeScript, RxJS-heavy state management, and a component library maintained in-house. Solid HTML/CSS fundamentals from earlier freelance work.

candidates.headline: Full-stack JavaScript engineer
candidates.description: End-to-end JavaScript developer - Node.js and Express on the backend with MongoDB as the primary store, React on the frontend. Comfortable across the whole stack on small-team projects where one person owns a feature top to bottom.

candidates.headline: Android app developer
candidates.description: Android developer with four years shipping consumer apps, originally in Java and increasingly in Kotlin over the last two years - Jetpack Compose, coroutines, and a strong focus on offline-first architecture.

candidates.headline: iOS developer
candidates.description: iOS engineer building consumer apps in Swift and SwiftUI for the past three years, with earlier UIKit experience. Comfortable with the full App Store release cycle and basic backend integration work.

candidates.headline: DevOps / cloud engineer
candidates.description: DevOps engineer running Kubernetes clusters on AWS for the last four years - Docker images, Helm charts, Jenkins pipelines and Ansible for configuration management. Also owns cost and reliability monitoring for the platform team.

candidates.headline: Site reliability & cloud infrastructure engineer
candidates.description: Infrastructure engineer focused on reliability - on-call rotations, incident response, and infrastructure-as-code across AWS. Terraform for provisioning day to day, with Docker and Kubernetes for the workload layer.

candidates.headline: Data scientist
candidates.description: Data scientist with a statistics background, three years building forecasting and churn models in Python. Heavy SQL for feature extraction against a PostgreSQL warehouse, plus regular stakeholder-facing reporting.

candidates.headline: Machine learning engineer
candidates.description: ML engineer focused on getting models into production rather than just training them - feature pipelines, model serving, and monitoring for drift. Python throughout, with most models trained using standard machine learning libraries against data pulled from SQL warehouses.

candidates.headline: QA automation engineer
candidates.description: QA engineer who moved fully into automation two years ago - Selenium and Cypress suites integrated into CI, plus a Python-based API test framework. Still does manual exploratory testing for anything UI-heavy before a release.

candidates.headline: Manual QA tester
candidates.description: Manual QA tester with strong domain knowledge of e-commerce checkout flows - test plan authoring, exploratory testing, and close collaboration with developers on bug triage. No coding background, purely manual testing so far.

candidates.headline: UX/UI designer
candidates.description: Product designer covering the full range from user research and wireframes through high-fidelity UI in Figma, with a solid Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator background from earlier brand-design work. Comfortable running usability sessions and translating findings into design changes.

candidates.headline: Cybersecurity analyst
candidates.description: Security analyst monitoring for and responding to incidents, with a background in network security assessments and vulnerability triage. Comfortable working from SIEM alerts through to a written incident report.

candidates.headline: Product manager
candidates.description: Product manager running discovery-to-delivery for a B2B SaaS product - roadmap ownership, stakeholder alignment, and close work with engineering in an Agile setup. Comfortable writing specs and reading data to validate decisions.

candidates.headline: Project manager, Agile delivery
candidates.description: Delivery-focused project manager running Scrum ceremonies for two engineering teams - sprint planning, backlog grooming, and stakeholder reporting. Background in software projects specifically, not general PM.

candidates.headline: .NET backend developer
candidates.description: Backend developer working primarily in C# on .NET, building internal line-of-business applications against SQL Server. Some exposure to Docker for packaging services but mostly deployed to on-premise Windows servers.
